Based on the retrieved excerpts, **clause 10.2** governs the response to incidents and nonconformities in ISO 45001.

## What ISO 45001 clause 10.2 adds beyond ISO 9001

When the trigger is an **incident** (such as a lost-time injury), clause 10.2 requires several OH&S-specific elements that go beyond a generic quality management corrective action process:

| ISO 45001-specific requirement | Clause 10.2 reference |
|-------------------------------|----------------------|
| **Evaluate need for corrective action with participation of workers and involvement of other relevant interested parties** | "evaluate — with participation of workers and involvement of other relevant interested parties — the need for corrective action" |
| **Review existing OH&S risk assessments** | "review existing OH&S risk assessments" |
| **Apply the hierarchy of controls** | "determine and implement corrective actions in line with the hierarchy of controls" |
| **Assess related OH&S risks before acting** | "assess related risks before acting" |
| **OH&S-specific communication** | "communicating this to relevant workers and interested parties" |

## Key distinction

While ISO 9001 focuses on correcting nonconformities affecting product/service quality, ISO 45001 clause 10.2 mandates that incident response must:
- Engage workers and interested parties in the evaluation
- Explicitly revisit risk assessments that may have failed to prevent the injury
- Apply the **hierarchy of controls** (elimination, substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls, PPE) rather than jumping to procedural fixes
- Assess whether the corrective action itself introduces new safety risks before implementation

The quality team's existing ISO 9001 process would need these adaptations to comply with ISO 45001 clause 10.2 for a lost-time injury.
